subject: Midterm growth multipliers & invoice ladder — ClearSight renewal
messages:
From: Priya Singh <psingh@clearsight.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Alvarez <mike.alvarez@clearsight.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-contract capacity uplift + invoicing ask

Hi Ava,

Quick note from our side — we expect usage to spike as we turn on three new product modules in July. We need to add ~30% committed capacity mid-contract and are evaluating how to do that without blowing fiscal Q3 cash flow. Two asks: (1) a short proposal for pricing multipliers (what multiple to charge for midterm add-ons vs annualized uplift), and (2) whether Redwood can support an "invoice ladder" (split payment across incremental invoices tied to ramp milestones).

We're targeting legal signoff by end of June if possible. Attached is a short one-pager describing expected ramp. Can you share a path and a rough numbers table? Also let me know procurement/PO timeline items we should plan for.

Thanks,
Priya Singh
VP, Cloud Ops — ClearSight Health
Attachments: ClearSight_Midterm_Request_0616.pdf

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <psingh@clearsight.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity uplift + invoicing ask

Hi Priya — thanks for the one-pager, that helps. High level approach below; I put Ben and Kimberly on copy to lock numbers and procurement path.

Options (quick summary):

1) Instant uplift (one-off add-on): Add 30% capacity as a discrete add-on invoiced up-front. Standard multiplier = 1.15x list for mid-contract buys. Good when you want immediate capacity and minimal contract changes.

2) Ramp + annualize (recommended if you plan to keep the capacity): We annualize the uplift for a blended effective rate. Example: 30% add now, convert to annual commit at a 1.05x multiplier (discount vs instant add), applied pro-rata across remaining term. This reduces immediate cash outlay.

3) Invoice ladder (custom schedule): Split payment into milestone-tied invoices (example: 40% at deploy, 30% at 60% of ramp, 30% on sustained usage). We can combine with a small uplift fee (1.08x) to cover billing complexity. This is useful for procurement cashflow smoothing.

Next steps I propose: Ben to share a short price table with the three options + suggested discount triggers; Kimberly to confirm whether legal needs an amendment or an addendum for the ladder option; if you prefer the ladder we can generate a redline-friendly draft and a DocuSign template.

I'll plan a 20-min call tomorrow to walk options if that helps — what time window works for you?

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | ava_chen@redwood.ai
Attachments: RDW-9581_draft_terms_ava_0617.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <psingh@clearsight.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity uplift + invoicing ask

Priya / team — sharing the concrete pricing ladder (table below) and a short note on approvals. See attached term sketch for the ladder wording.

Proposed pricing multipliers (examples for 30% uplift on current commit):
- Instant add-on (single invoice): multiplier 1.15x list -> estimated incremental MRR $12,450
- Annualize & blend: multiplier 1.05x list pro-rated to remaining term -> estimated incremental MRR $9,600 (lower upfront)
- Invoice ladder (3-way milestone): multiplier 1.08x list -> invoice schedule example: 40% at deployment, 30% at 60% ramp (calendar), 30% on sustained usage for 30 days.

Approval items & timing:
- Legal: contract amendment or one-page addendum (Kim to confirm language & timeline) — target 5 business days for simple addendum.
- Procurement: PO referencing RDW-9581 + invoice ladder terms; finance ok with three-invoice schedules once we have milestone definitions.

If you want, I can produce a final numbers sheet with dollars tied to your current usage baseline (send a quick snapshot of current committed units).

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachments: RDW-9581_pricing_sketch_0617.xlsx (stub)

From: Priya Singh <psingh@clearsight.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Alvarez <mike.alvarez@clearsight.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity uplift + invoicing ask

Thanks Ava / Ben — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. ClearSight prefers Option 3 (Invoice ladder) but with one change: split the ladder into three invoices across the next 90 days (rather than two calendar milestones) to align with our product launch schedule. We accept the 1.08x ladder multiplier.

Action items we need from Redwood:
- Produce a 1-page addendum with the ladder wording and explicit invoice dates (we'll provide launch milestones).
- A DocuSign-ready agreement we can sign (legal wants a link).
- A final pricing table with exact dollar amounts tied to our current committed units so procurement can issue the PO.

If you can get the addendum and DocuSign template to us by EOD Monday (6/21), we'll route to our legal and finance and aim to sign by 6/30.

Thanks,
Priya Singh
VP, Cloud Ops — ClearSight Health
